title: Lower Manhattan Waterfront Walk
description: A scenic loop along the southern tip of Manhattan, tracing the Hudson and East River waterfronts past Battery Park, the historic harbor, and the financial district's landmark architecture.

stops.title: Harlem Meer
stops.transcription: Welcome to Harlem Meer, a peaceful lake at the northeastern corner of Central Park. While Midtown Manhattan gets most of the attention, this quieter section offers a completely different atmosphere. Look across the water and you'll often spot turtles, herons, and local anglers enjoying one of the park's hidden gems.

stops.title: Charles A. Dana Discovery Center
stops.transcription: This visitor center serves as the gateway to the northern part of Central Park. It hosts exhibitions, educational programs, and community events. Many visitors never venture this far north, making this one of the park's least crowded areas.

stops.title: Conservatory Garden Entrance
stops.transcription: Just west of your route lies the Conservatory Garden, Central Park's only formal garden. Inspired by European landscape traditions, it contrasts sharply with the park's naturalistic design. Depending on the season, you'll find thousands of blooming flowers and some of the most beautiful photography locations in New York.

stops.title: Vanderbilt Gate
stops.transcription: These ornate iron gates once stood outside a Fifth Avenue mansion belonging to the Vanderbilt family. They were later relocated here and now form one of Central Park's grandest entrances. The decorative details are easy to miss, so take a moment to appreciate the craftsmanship.

stops.title: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir Overlook
stops.transcription: The path now approaches the famous Reservoir. Originally built as part of New York's water system, it is now one of the city's favorite running routes. The open water creates remarkable skyline views that change dramatically throughout the day.

stops.title: Engineer's Gate
stops.transcription: Engineer's Gate marks one of the principal entrances to Central Park from the Upper East Side. Nearby stands a statue honoring engineer and inventor John Ericsson. This area also offers one of the easiest access points between the city streets and the park's interior.

stops.title: Cleopatra's Needle
stops.transcription: Standing nearby is one of the oldest objects in New York City. Cleopatra's Needle is an authentic Egyptian obelisk carved more than three thousand years ago. It arrived in New York in 1881 after a complex transatlantic journey and remains one of the city's most extraordinary historical artifacts.

stops.title: Kerbs Memorial Boathouse
stops.transcription: This charming boathouse sits beside Conservatory Water, a pond famous for model sailboats. For generations, New Yorkers have come here to race miniature boats across the water. The scene feels surprisingly timeless despite the skyscrapers surrounding the park.

stops.title: The Pond
stops.transcription: As you approach the southern end of Central Park, you'll encounter The Pond. Designed to create the illusion of a remote woodland landscape, it serves as a transition between nature and the city. The contrast between the water, trees, and surrounding towers is one of the park's defining views.

stops.title: Gapstow Bridge
stops.transcription: Your walk concludes at Gapstow Bridge. This stone bridge is one of the most photographed locations in Central Park. Looking north, you'll see the pond and tree-lined pathways. Looking south, you'll see the skyline of Midtown Manhattan rising above the park. It's the perfect place to appreciate how Central Park blends nature and city life.
